results.title: A Museum for the future - Museu Calouste Gulbenkian
results.description: More than 55 years after its inauguration, the Gulbenkian Museum has closed for renovation works, reopening in July 2026.

highlights:
[A Museum for the future]

More than 55 years after its inauguration, the Gulbenkian Museum has closed for renovation works, reopening in July 2026. This project will ensure the best possible conditions to preserve and display the extraordinary Calouste Gulbenkian Collection for many decades to come.

The renovation includes modernising climate control, lighting, and security systems, enhancing the visitor experience, and refining the museum’s architectural harmony – always respecting its original vision.

…

While the Museum is temporarily closed, the Collection remains accessible to the public. The Great Works exhibition will showcase 200 masterpieces at the Gulbenkian Foundation’s Headquarters from 12 April to 1 September. Additionally, four essential works will also be on display in British Art – Converge until 21 July.

Starting July 18, visitors will be able to explore a space that has until now been inaccessible to the public. Adjacent to the Greece, Rome, and Mesopotamia gallery, the numismatics cabinet – which for many years served as the base for research on the coin collection – will now be open to visitors.

…

[Behind the scenes of the Gulbenkian Museum renovation > A Particular Taste]

From July, with the reopening of the Museum, part of this nucleus will once again be on display. An opportunity to see up close what Gulbenkian chose to keep.

results.description: The result of an unprecedented partnership, this exhibition is taking place at a time when the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum building is closed for renovation until July 2026.

highlights:
[Dialogues]

The result of an unprecedented partnership, this exhibition is taking place at a time when the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum building is closed for renovation until July 2026. This exhibition will also serve as a pretext for a renovation of the Machado de Castro National Museum.

The exhibition will run from 31 October 2025 to 22 February 2026 on the first floor of the former Episcopal Palace of the Machado de Castro National Museum.
